query_text: When is my screening visit?
top_responses: Your screening visit is the first appointment where the study team checks if you meet the eligibility criteria.
The screening visit usually happens before any study procedures begin.
You will be contacted by the study coordinator to schedule your screening appointment.

query_text: What happens on Day 0?
top_responses: Day 0 is when you officially start the study and receive your first study-related procedures or medication.
Baseline tests and first dosing may occur on Day 0.
The team will review the study plan with you on Day 0.

query_text: How long does Visit 5 take?
top_responses: Visit length varies, but most visits last between 30 minutes and 2 hours.
Your coordinator can give you a specific time estimate for Visit 5.
Some visits take longer if lab tests or imaging are included.

query_text: Can I drink alcohol during the study?
top_responses: Alcohol use may be restricted during the study. Follow the instructions given by the study team.
Some studies allow limited alcohol, others prohibit it.
Ask your coordinator before drinking alcohol.

query_text: Am I allowed to take supplements?
top_responses: Some supplements are not allowed. Always check with the study team first.
Certain vitamins or herbs can interfere with the study drug.
Provide a list of all supplements to your coordinator.

query_text: Can I take ibuprofen for pain?
top_responses: Certain pain medications like ibuprofen may be restricted.
Some studies allow only acetaminophen instead.
Always ask the study doctor before taking painkillers.

query_text: What side effects should I expect?
top_responses: Side effects vary by study and are explained in the consent form.
You may receive a list of known risks.
Report any symptoms to the study staff immediately.

query_text: Will I get paid for participating?
top_responses: Participants may receive reimbursement for time and travel.
Compensation is based on completed visits.
Your coordinator can explain the payment schedule.

query_text: Can I leave the study early?
top_responses: You can leave the study at any time without penalty.
You do not need to give a reason.
Tell the study team if you decide to stop.

query_text: Who do I contact in an emergency?
top_responses: You will receive emergency contact information for the study doctor.
Call the emergency number in your consent form.
If urgent, seek care and notify the study team.

query_text: How many visits are there in total?
top_responses: The number of visits is defined in the study protocol.
Your coordinator can review the visit schedule with you.
Some studies include screening, treatment, and follow-up visits.

query_text: Can I reschedule a study visit?
top_responses: Yes, contact your coordinator as soon as possible to reschedule.
Some visits have time windows defined by the protocol.
The study team will try to accommodate your schedule.

query_text: What if I miss a visit?
top_responses: Contact the study team immediately if you miss a visit.
Missed visits must be documented in the study records.
Your coordinator will advise you on next steps.

query_text: Do I have to attend all follow-up visits?
top_responses: Yes, follow-up visits are important for your safety and study results.
Try to attend all scheduled visits.
If you cannot attend, notify the team in advance.

query_text: Will I have blood drawn at every visit?
top_responses: Blood draws depend on the study schedule.
Some visits require labs, others do not.
Your coordinator can explain when blood will be taken.

query_text: Do I need to fast before my lab tests?
top_responses: Some lab tests require fasting. The study team will tell you if this applies to you.
Your coordinator will give you instructions before your visit.
Follow all preparation guidelines provided by the study staff.

query_text: What happens to my blood samples after collection?
top_responses: Samples are labeled and stored according to the study protocol.
They may be analyzed in a central laboratory.
All samples are handled under strict confidentiality rules.

query_text: Do I have to return unused study medication?
top_responses: Yes, you must return any unused study medication at each visit.
This helps the team track dosing and compliance.
Never share your study drug with anyone else.

query_text: What should I do if I miss a dose?
top_responses: Do not double up on doses. Contact the study team for instructions.
The coordinator will advise you on how to proceed.
Missed doses must be documented.

query_text: Can someone else take my study medication?
top_responses: No, the study medication is only for you.
Sharing study drugs is not allowed.
Return any unused medication to the study site.

query_text: How is my safety monitored during the study?
top_responses: Your safety is monitored by the investigator and study staff.
Some studies also have an independent safety committee.
All side effects are reviewed regularly.

query_text: Has this study been approved by an ethics committee?
top_responses: Yes, the study must be approved by an ethics committee before it starts.
Approval ensures participant rights and safety are protected.
You can ask your coordinator for more details.

query_text: Can the study procedures change after I join?
top_responses: Any changes must be approved before being implemented.
You will be informed if procedures change.
You may be asked to re-sign the consent form.

query_text: What is re-consent?
top_responses: Re-consent means signing an updated consent form with new information.
It happens if new risks or changes arise.
You always have the right to ask questions before signing.

query_text: Will my medical records be reviewed?
top_responses: Authorized study staff and regulators may review your records.
This is done to ensure data accuracy and safety.
Your privacy is protected at all times.

query_text: What is a monitoring visit?
top_responses: Monitoring visits check that the study is being conducted properly.
Monitors review data, consent forms, and procedures.
These visits help ensure compliance with regulations.

query_text: Are there audits or inspections?
top_responses: Yes, authorities may inspect study sites.
Audits help ensure the study follows all rules.
The site must always be inspection-ready.

query_text: When will study results be available?
top_responses: Results are available after the study is completed and analyzed.
Timelines depend on the study design.
You can ask the team if results will be shared with participants.

query_text: Can I see the study findings?
top_responses: Some studies share summaries of results with participants.
Ask your coordinator if and when results will be provided.
Published results may be available publicly.

query_text: How long are my study records kept?
top_responses: Study records are stored securely for the required retention period.
Retention timelines follow regulatory requirements.
The sponsor is responsible for long-term archiving.
